lenses.label: SPHERE/ZIMPOL · polarised dust, 2024
lenses.title: Polarised dust around Betelgeuse in 2024
lenses.description: The degree of linear polarisation VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL measured in the V band on 3 December 2024, placed in the plane of the sky through the star and spread along the line of sight by the scattering-angle efficiency of polarised light. The patches are dust. Depth is a stated convention, not a measurement, and nothing finer than the 16 milliarcsecond beam is in the data.
lenses.summary: Measured polarised light from dust one to 4.5 stellar radii out; its depth is a convention.

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: Not measured; a plane-of-sky slab spread by scattering angle

lenses.label: Great Dimming clump · December 2019
lenses.title: The dust clump of the Great Dimming
lenses.description: The dust clump Montargès et al. fitted with RADMC-3D to the images of the Great Dimming, drawn from the numbers they published for December 2019: a sphere of uniform density south and slightly west of the star and between it and us. It is drawn as starlight scattered by that dust, so only the illumination varies across it. This is a model fitted to images, not an image.
lenses.summary: A published model of the dust that dimmed the southern hemisphere in December 2019.

facts.label: Model
facts.value: RADMC-3D sphere of constant density, Montargès et al. 2021, Extended Data Table 3

facts.label: Centre and radius
facts.value: (−1.9, −3.0, +12.5) au along right ascension, declination and toward Earth; radius 6.5 au

facts.label: Dust density
facts.value: 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ g cm⁻³ in MgFeSiO₄ grains centred on 0.21 µm

facts.label: Epoch
facts.value: December 2019, the only optimised solution the paper reports
